description: Search a buying signal like the Sinais screen: companies hiring a role (hiring), recent funding rounds (funding: periodDays 7/30/90/180), company news (news), companies showing a technology (tech), Brazilian company registry events (cnpj), companies that started a construction (construction), closed-lost CRM deals (crm) or people new in a role (job_change: jobTitle, periodDays 30/60/90, location, industry, companySizes; domains narrows to the user's accounts for "decisor novo na conta"; move new_company or promotion; each result is a person with the company they joined, the title and the month), companies whose team grew (growth: minGrowthPct, months 6 or 12, location, industry, companySizes; only companies with a LinkedIn page) or companies running ads now (ads: query, a theme in the advertisers' words, read in Meta's Ad Library in Brazil; or domains, up to 10 of the user's accounts checked on Google's Ads Transparency Center). cnpj.event picks what happened: opening (new CNPJ, the default), branch (opened a branch), mei_exit (left the MEI; stayedInSimples = became an ME), simples_exit (left the Simples Nacional), new_partner (a partner joined the QSA), gov_contract (signed a public contract, PNCP), debt_new (new federal active debt, PGFN), and from the Receita edition comparison capital_up, address_change, cnae_change. Every event but opening needs location with a state ("Curitiba, PR", "SC") or industry. construction is "Iniciou uma construção": companies that registered a construction project at the Receita's CNO; location with a state is required, minAreaM2 is optional, periodDays 7/30/90; cite Receita Federal (CNO). Each result's title already states the fact with its date, and facts.sourceProvider names its public source. Up to 25 results per search, set by limit (without it: 2 for hiring, funding, news, tech, cnpj and construction, 10 for the others). Charged per result returned: 4 credits each (8 for a hiring company found by the wider job-board search), 2 for cnpj and construction, 24 for tech, 4 per person for job_change, 2 for growth, 4 for ads, CRM free; the most a search can cost is limit × price. tech finds companies by evidence such as job posts, not proof that a company uses a technology today. Companies that run an ERP (TOTVS, SAP Business One, Omie...) have no search here: they come from a "Usa ERP" market monitor (category erp). provider is optional and picks one source: funding takes company_data (the default, filters by location and size) or announcements (round announcements only); tech takes job_posts (the default, tools named in job posts) or website (the company's own pages). A free signal: news takes what (what happened, in the user's words, e.g. "lançou produto em refil") instead of categories, searched in the Brazilian press. Hiring, news and cnpj take rules ("quem serve", up to three, e.g. "é fabricante de bens de consumo embalados"): twice the number asked is searched and each company is checked against them before it is delivered, 2 credits per company checked on top of the result price. Also, companies by what their own site and e-mail domain load (site_tech: technologies, any of hubspot (HubSpot), rdstation (RD Station), rdstation_crm (RD Station CRM), salesforce (Salesforce), pardot (Pardot (Salesforce)), zendesk (Zendesk), intercom (Intercom), freshdesk (Freshdesk), sensedata (SenseData), mailchimp (Mailchimp), sendgrid (SendGrid), google_workspace (Google Workspace), microsoft_365 (Microsoft 365), hotjar (Hotjar), clarity (Microsoft Clarity), gtm (Google Tag Manager), linkedin_insight (LinkedIn Insight Tag), meta_pixel (Pixel da Meta); change uses (on the site now), adopted (new since the last reading) or removed (gone since the last reading; adopted and removed need a monitor or a site read before); domains, up to 25 of the user's accounts, read for free and charged 2 credits per company found; or a market by location, industry and companySizes, where each company checked costs 2 credits whether it uses the technology or not). site_tech is the signal for "who uses HubSpot / RD Station / Salesforce"; tech is not. Free, from the user's own data: email_engagement (people in the user's campaigns who opened at least minOpens 1-3 e-mails in periodDays 7/14/30 and did not reply, each with the next step to take; campaignIds narrows it), followers (people following every LinkedIn account connected in the workspace, newest first, jobTitle narrows by headline; a monitor started with start "future" delivers only new followers; profile views are not available) and competitor_intent (people ranked by how much they engaged with the recent posts of the competitors' LinkedIn company pages: comment 3, reaction 1, +2 per other competitor, +2 if in the last 7 days; minScore, jobTitle; competitors adds pages by name to the ones the company profile names (profileCompetitors false reads only these; for a Brazilian sales or outbound tool, typical competitors are Ramper, Econodata, Meetime, Exact Sales, Agendor, RD Station); the competitors' own staff and the user's company are left out; country (ISO, default the workspace's, "any" for all) lists people located there first, unknown location after, and drops people located elsewhere. The pages are read at most once a day per workspace, at Nock's cost, capped at about US$ 2 a read). From public pages, 2 credits per company: reviews (stores that reviewed a competitor's app in Nuvemshop's app store: apps, up to 5 app slugs or URLs; maxRating 1-5, 5 keeps every review; periodDays 30/90/365) and trade_show (the companies on a trade show's public exhibitor list: url of the list; name). hiring_surge: companies whose job postings of the last 30 days at least double the monthly pace of the 60 days before (minRecent, default 3), overall or in one area (vendas, marketing, tecnologia, pessoas, financas, operacoes, atendimento, juridico); mode accounts with domains (up to 10 of the user's companies, 2 credits per posting read, up to 20 per company) or mode history (free, from the postings the workspace's hiring signals already saved). crm_events reads the workspace's connected CRM (provider hubspot or salesforce, connectionId as the crm signal takes it): event stalled_deal (open deals with no change for staleDays 14/30/60), renewal_due (won deals whose first anniversary is 60 to 90 days ahead), field_condition (a deal field, its internal name, equal to value), all free; contact_moved checks up to 10 contacts of customers in the CRM mirror for a move to another company, 4 credits per move found, nothing when nobody moved (search only, not a monitor). own: the signals the user's product and events sent to a sheet's webhook (kinds trial_started, trial_ending, usage_spike, usage_drop, invited_team, event_registered, event_attended; periodDays 7/30/90), free. Setting one up takes a sheet webhook (Planilhas, Webhook) that receives JSON with signal (one of the kinds), email or company_domain, and optional name, event_name, detail; Segment, Mixpanel, n8n, Sympla, Even3 and Zoom can send it. Executives hired are found as news with what (e.g. "contratou novo CEO, diretor ou VP") in the Brazilian press.

rules.description: Up to three rules each company the signal finds must meet, checked one by one with evidence before it is delivered (e.g. "é fabricante de bens de consumo embalados"). Each company checked costs the verification credits.
